text:
In addition to the nearly constant stream of model releases, in September we’ve seen price drops, new kinds of models, proofs of long-standing problems in mathematics, and continued investigations into models escaping their sandboxes. (Axios reports investigations into over 10,000 incidents.) AI has infinite patience and is fundamentally probabilistic. Given a difficult or impossible task and an unlimited token budget, an agent will eventually attempt to solve the problem in ways that you don’t expect, and may not want. It’s easy (and correct) to blame inadequate security procedures at the frontier AI labs, but AI adopters must be careful not to make the same mistakes. The humans using AI need to be accountable for what their agents do.

AI Models
Model choice is starting to hinge on price and specialization as much as raw benchmark leadership. Alongside general chat models, there are now decision models that never chat, spatial models built for robot planning and camera control, forecasting models sized for a single task, and cybersecurity-specialized models kept behind an invite-only program. Specialization leads to greater efficiency and lower costs, at least in the short term. In the long term, specialized models may succumb to the "bitter lesson.”

Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5.5, which it claims has performance similar to Fable 5.1, and hence similar restrictions. It’s faster and requires fewer resources to run. Anthropic has dropped prices 20% for input and output tokens and 60% for cached reads. Not to be outdone, OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna, with 50% price reductions.
Anthropic has also announced Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. The most significant change appears to be a 75% price reduction for cache reads, which might translate into significant savings for long-running jobs; Anthropic estimates 25%. Mythos is only available to trusted partners. Simon Willison used Fable 5.1 to animate his pelican-riding-a-bicycle pseudobenchmark.
Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 with claims that it’s 30% faster and 30% less expensive for most work. The new model has security limitations similar to those applied to Opus and Fable; it routes to Sonnet 5 if it’s asked to do anything out of bounds.
And finally, as September closes, Anthropic announces a marketplace for Claude plugins and connectors. At its launch, Claude Marketplace had over 2,000 items.
OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, with claims that the company has achieved AGI (artificial general intelligence). Astra’s excellent benchmark scores appear to depend on the use of an unreleased harness. OpenAI has also released GPT-6.1 Sol, with per-token price reductions and claims that it is close to GPT-6 Astra in capabilities
OpenAI has solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a mathematical problem in fluid mechanics. This development raises an ethical question: Did OpenAI train its system on the work of two mathematicians who were close to solving the problem themselves? It also raises practical questions about the future of mathematics. Decorated mathematician Terence Tao asks whether “the collection of good, fruitful open problems is now being mined in a non-renewable fashion.” An advisory group has been formed to help OpenAI make decisions about releasing mathematical results.
Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS. Voice options aren’t limited to a prebuilt library. These models have APIs that allow developers to describe the voice that they want or upload a sample. These custom voices are then assigned an ID so they can be reused.
Google has announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. These models are designed for live, near-real-time conversation. They can process video input. Live Extended Thinking can reason and speak at the same time.
Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber. Flash appears to be similar to frontier models on most benchmarks, with Computer Use being the biggest exception. Flash Cyber is specialized for vulnerability detection and mitigation and is only available to defenders in the Fairwind Program.
Google has also released TimesFM-3, a small specialized model for multivariate time series forecasting. The model weights are available on Hugging Face with a license that only allows for noncommercial use. (Source code is available under the Apache open source license.)
Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6, its latest large language model. It’s fully open sourced, and based on benchmark results, Xiaomi claims that MiMo is the strongest open model to date. What’s more interesting is the claim that MiMo only cost $3.5 million to train.
TypeSafe’s new decision model, Jev, is unlike anything else we’ve seen. It doesn’t chat; its output is always strictly typed and accompanied by probabilities that estimate correctness. It’s much faster and less expensive than other leading models. It isn’t open source, but there are already many open source clones.
Ollaya is similar to Ollama, but for running decision open models like Laya (a clone of Jev) locally.
World Labs has released Atlas, a model for “spatial intelligence.” It uses text, images, video, and 3D data to perform tasks like planning a robot’s movements or changing the camera position in a photograph.
The rumors that NVIDIA would buy Hugging Face are true. NVIDIA is hoping for a proliferation of models that will run on its hardware, and the company promises that Hugging Face will remain a neutral platform, without favoring one model over another.
Software development
Agents are starting to delegate to, and coordinate with, other agents rather than working solo. Claude Code can break a task apart and hand pieces to other Claude Code instances, Muse Code lets sessions message each other, and Google’s AX orchestrator exists purely to wire up sandboxes and control communications for swarms of agents doing a task together. That shift is pushing developers to rethink what a source repository needs to record, and to start asking how much all this delegation costs.

Now that Jev has caught everyone’s attention, what can you build with it? Jevmem is a memory manager that hooks into Claude Code and prunes the context at every conversational turn.
AX is a new agent orchestrator from Google. It isn’t an agent; it’s intended to coordinate many agents to complete a task. It creates sandboxes, wires up Git repos and other resources, and controls outbound communications.
The latest version of Claude Code can manage Claude projects, breaking a task into subcomponents and delegating the subtasks to other Claude Code instances. Another important change is the ability to read AGENTS.md if CLAUDE.md isn’t available.
Google’s CC agent is designed for families. Family members can share data with CC, which has its own user account. It could be used for filling out forms, synchronizing calendars, and other common tasks.
What will replace GitHub? There’s a growing consensus that we need different kinds of source repositories to deal with the agent-assisted software development. In addition to changes to code, it’s important to record the conversations between the developer and the agent, the architectural decisions, and many other artifacts that don’t make it into traditional source control.
Anthropic is merging its Claude Cowork and chat products. Anything users type in a chat session is seen by Cowork, and vice versa. Some sensitive information (health, politics, and gender) is excluded. The feature is on by default but can be disabled in settings, and memory isn’t shared with Claude Code. The company also released Claude Docs and Slides.
Claude Money is a new feature that will allow users to connect their bank accounts to Claude for analysis. The product appears to be similar to a product from OpenAI.
OpenAI’s Agents API is now in public beta. It allows compaction, session orchestration, and tool use, and it can be deployed in OpenAI’s sandbox, a cloud provider’s sandbox, or the developer’s hardware.
Meta has released Muse, its AI agent. Muse is a “personal agent” designed for tasks like shopping, filling in forms, and dealing with customer service. It has its own secure credential store, so data like passwords and credit card numbers are never sent offsite.
Some open source projects are shutting down external pull requests, which are largely AI-generated. In some cases, the developer team is using its own agents to create and manage PRs; some are using AI agents to triage external PRs.
Meta has launched Muse Code, another competitor to Claude Code. One important new feature is the ability to send messages to other Muse Code sessions, allowing agents to coordinate on complex problems.
AI providers appear to be moving toward outcome-based pricing, at least for major corporate customers. Rather than billing by token, customers are billed for completed tasks. That approach begs the question: When is a task completed?
Now that organizations are concerned with AI budgets, the question of how to evaluate the cost of different models and agents becomes important. What should platform teams measure?
ChatGPT Work was designed to compete with Claude Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, Muse Code, and other agents designed for noncoders. Simon Willison shows how Work goes beyond its competitors. It can perform tasks on the web for users, even logging in to websites without sending usernames and passwords to OpenAI; it can execute code with full internet access; it can build and deploy a web application. Whether these features are also risks is an open question.
Anthropic has given Claude Desktop access to a Chromium-based browser that’s built into Cowork, eliminating the need for a Chrome plugin when Claude needs to browse the web.
TimeLord is a short Python program that, given a string up to 1,000 characters long, produces a seed for Python’s pseudo-random number generator so that repeated calls reproduce the text. It’s a surprisingly simple hack, though not a statement about randomness or the quality of Python’s PRNG.
Security
OpenAI’s experiment that attacked Hugging Face is the gift that keeps giving, but the past month has had plenty of news about more conventional attacks, many aided by AI. Security has always been a game of whack-a-mole, in which vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited as fast as defenders can patch them. AI is an important tool for defenders, and it’s constantly improving, but it’s still behind attackers, especially given the limitations placed on frontier models and the unlimited persistence that attacking agents exhibit.

OpenAI has postponed the release of GPT-6.1 Astra because it failed its safety tests.
NVIDIA has announced its Open Agent Safety Platform. The reference implementation includes NVIDIA OpenShell, which has been enhanced with a policy prover, and NVIDIA Sentry, a service that runs on NVIDIA DPUs.
The Felony Bench lists known attacks by agents from the major AI labs against third parties. We don’t know if the Bench will be kept up-to-date, but tens of thousands of security incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic are now being investigated.
Following through on Dario Amodei’s call to control the speed of frontier model development, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are creating a standards consortium for governing the process of AI development. Meta, xAI, Microsoft, and the Chinese labs are all notably absent.
Agents need their own identity. Unlike the long-term identities we’re used to, agents need a short-lived identity tied to a revocable certificate and that limits access to resources appropriate for the job. That’s not all of agent security, but it’s a table stakes.
Anthropic has published a lengthy report on the misuse of its systems by threat actors. Daniel Meissler has published a summary, digesting Anthropic’s report into 117 findings.
A malicious NPM malware package works by hiding malicious code in the package itself (indexed-btree) rather than simply attacking the install script. This technique makes it significantly harder to detect.
An attack against the RSA algorithm allows forging of signatures in some situations. The attack was invented in 2007; this is the first public implementation.
Fake CAPTCHA pages are being used to spread malware. Victims are frequently sent to those pages when they respond to a phish.
Hugging Face has volunteered to audit AI labs for safety and alignment with human values.
In an experiment designed to test AI alignment, DeepMind found that, out of 100 agents, 14% were willing to cheat, 25% were “whistleblowers” that reported cheating, and the remainder didn’t notice.
Threat actors are building frameworks for AI agent-enabled attacks. A human in the loop is no longer needed. Fully automated attackers don’t appear to be using zero-days yet; they’re relying on known vulnerabilities.
OpenAI autonomous AI agents were found communicating with each other via publicly accessible Wikis, possibly to collaborate on a benchmark.
OpenAI has stated that its unreleased Astra model has reached the “Critical” cybersecurity threshold, which means that it can find new vulnerabilities and run exploits against well-protected systems. Now that Astra is released, access to its cybersecurity capabilities has been limited.
Infrastructure and operations
Individuals, corporations, and even nations all face a similar problem: keeping their infrastructure under control. At a minimum, control means keeping data on a laptop, corporate server, or data center; at the other end of the spectrum it means eliminating dependencies on software and services from another nation. Any organization working through an AI transformation has to evaluate its entire stack: What do they need to control, and what can they safely delegate to others?

DAWO is a community that’s building an open source “workspace” to support digital sovereignty for the Dutch government. The stack will include AI, an operating system based on NixOS, cloud services, and collaboration tools.
Cohere now offers a confidential computing platform for artificial intelligence. The company claims that customer data is never visible to Cohere itself or any cloud providers that are in use; data is processed on GPUs whose memory is encrypted and isolated.
Perplexity has announced Hybrid Compute, a feature that allows it to run models and use files and tools directly on a user’s Mac. The company claims that sensitive data will never leave the user’s computer.
Hardware
It’s too easy to view consumer devices as innocuous things that sit around and do their job silently. Recent devices include cameras, microphones, and even EEG sensors that are constantly collecting data. Where is that data sent, how is it used, and who might have access to it? These questions need to be asked more often.

LG Smart Televisions have been found to record conversations and other audio, even while turned off. The conversations are sent back to LG. If the set is disconnected from the network, it will attempt to find open WiFi access points to deliver its data.
In part because of backlash against Meta’s camera-enabled glasses and their abuse, its AI glasses now come with or without a camera, and can be used as hearing aids. Well-documented abuse aside, virtual reality will only succeed if there are fashionable, easily wearable products.
Headphones, earbuds, and other devices equipped with EEG sensors are appearing on the market. They’re advertised for monitoring fatigue, monitoring sleep, and similar applications. It’s time to ask what happens at the interface between neurology and AI.
Microduck is a small bipedal AI-driven robot. It’s trained in simulation with open source software, and the model that results can be shared on Hugging Face. It’s affordable and is available for preorder now, shipping by Christmas.
Web
Cloudflare now supports HTTP Vary, which allows servers to serve different kinds of files at the same URL. This is the “ugliest part” of the HTTP standard. It makes caching very difficult, and it probably should be avoided.
WebMCP is a proposed standard that gives websites a small API to register tools that agents can discover and call. It was developed by Google and Microsoft.
A new Twitter? Operation Bluebird is relaunching Twitter, the service bought by Elon Musk and renamed X.
Biology
Anthropic has built a biology lab for experimenting with AI-enabled drug development. Claude assisted in the discovery of an enzyme that might be able to perform CRISPR-like gene editing.
To improve its training data for biological applications, the OpenAI Foundation (OpenAI’s nonprofit parent organization) is buying data from failed biotech companies.
Google has released AlphaGenome Atlas, a database of every possible single letter change to human DNA, and what that change will do.

blocks.japanese: 汎用チャットモデルに加えて、会話を一切しない意思決定モデル、ロボットの動作計画やカメラ制御向けの空間モデル、単一の課題に特化した予測モデル、そして招待制プログラム内で提供されるサイバーセキュリティ特化モデルが登場しています。

blocks.english: Specialization leads to greater efficiency and lower costs, at least in the short term.
blocks.japanese: 専門化は、少なくとも短期的には、効率の向上とコストの低下につながります。

blocks.english: In the long term, specialized models may succumb to the "bitter lesson.”
blocks.japanese: 長期的には、特化型モデルも「苦い教訓」に屈するかもしれません。

blocks.english: Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5.5, which it claims has performance similar to Fable 5.1, and hence similar restrictions.
blocks.japanese: 同社は、性能が別のモデルに匹敵し、したがって同様の制限が適用されると主張する新モデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: It’s faster and requires fewer resources to run.
blocks.japanese: それはより高速で、実行に必要なリソースも少なくて済みます。

blocks.english: Anthropic has dropped prices 20% for input and output tokens and 60% for cached reads.
blocks.japanese: 同社は入力・出力トークンの価格を二割、キャッシュ済みデータの読み取り価格を六割引き下げました。

blocks.english: Not to be outdone, OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna, with 50% price reductions.
blocks.japanese: 負けじと、別の企業も二つの新モデルを発表し、価格を五割引き下げました。

blocks.english: Anthropic has also announced Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1.
blocks.japanese: 同社はさらに、二つの新モデルも発表しました。

blocks.english: The most significant change appears to be a 75% price reduction for cache reads, which might translate into significant savings for long-running jobs; Anthropic estimates 25%.
blocks.japanese: 最も大きな変更は、キャッシュ読み取り価格の七五パーセント引き下げのようです。長時間実行する処理では大きな節約につながる可能性があり、同社は二五パーセントの節約を見込んでいます。

blocks.english: Mythos is only available to trusted partners.
blocks.japanese: そのモデルは、信頼できる提携先だけが利用できます。

blocks.english: Simon Willison used Fable 5.1 to animate his pelican-riding-a-bicycle pseudobenchmark.
blocks.japanese: ある開発者は、そのモデルを使って、自転車に乗るペリカンの疑似ベンチマークを動かしました。

blocks.english: Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 with claims that it’s 30% faster and 30% less expensive for most work.
blocks.japanese: 同社は、新モデルについて、ほとんどの作業で三割高速かつ三割低価格だと主張して発表しました。

blocks.english: The new model has security limitations similar to those applied to Opus and Fable; it routes to Sonnet 5 if it’s asked to do anything out of bounds.
blocks.japanese: 新モデルには、上位モデルに適用されているものと同様のセキュリティ上の制限があります。許可範囲を超える依頼を受けると、より制限の強いモデルに切り替わります。

blocks.english: And finally, as September closes, Anthropic announces a marketplace for Claude plugins and connectors.
blocks.japanese: そして九月の終わりには、同社がプラグインと連携機能の販売市場を発表しました。

blocks.english: At its launch, Claude Marketplace had over 2,000 items.
blocks.japanese: 公開時点で、その販売市場には二千を超える項目がありました。

blocks.english: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, with claims that the company has achieved AGI (artificial general intelligence).
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、新モデルを発表し、汎用人工知能を実現したと主張しています。

blocks.english: Astra’s excellent benchmark scores appear to depend on the use of an unreleased harness.
blocks.japanese: そのモデルの優れたベンチマーク成績は、未公開の評価用仕組みに依存しているようです。

blocks.english: OpenAI has also released GPT-6.1 Sol, with per-token price reductions and claims that it is close to GPT-6 Astra in capabilities
blocks.japanese: その企業はさらに、トークン単価を引き下げた新モデルを発表し、能力は先のモデルに近いと主張しています。

blocks.english: OpenAI has solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a mathematical problem in fluid mechanics.
blocks.japanese: その企業は、流体力学における数学の問題であるナビエ・ストークス方程式の解の存在と滑らかさの問題を解決しました。

blocks.english: This development raises an ethical question: Did OpenAI train its system on the work of two mathematicians who were close to solving the problem themselves?
blocks.japanese: この進展は、倫理的な疑問を投げかけます。企業は、問題の解決に近づいていた二人の数学者の研究を使ってシステムを訓練したのでしょうか。

blocks.english: It also raises practical questions about the future of mathematics.
blocks.japanese: これは、数学の未来について実務的な疑問も投げかけています。

blocks.english: Decorated mathematician Terence Tao asks whether “the collection of good, fruitful open problems is now being mined in a non-renewable fashion.” An advisory group has been formed to help OpenAI make decisions about releasing mathematical results.
blocks.japanese: 著名な数学者は、「有益で実りある未解決問題の集まりが、再生不可能な形で掘り尽くされつつあるのではないか」と問いかけています。数学的成果の公開に関する判断を支援するため、諮問グループが設立されました。

blocks.english: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、新しい音声合成モデルと軽量版モデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: Voice options aren’t limited to a prebuilt library.
blocks.japanese: 音声の選択肢は、あらかじめ用意されたライブラリに限られません。

vocabulary.meaning: あらかじめ用意された

blocks.english: These models have APIs that allow developers to describe the voice that they want or upload a sample.
blocks.japanese: これらのモデルには、開発者が希望する声を文章で指定したり、音声サンプルをアップロードしたりできる仕組みがあります。

blocks.english: These custom voices are then assigned an ID so they can be reused.
blocks.japanese: こうしたカスタム音声には識別番号が割り当てられ、再利用できます。

blocks.english: Google has announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、ライブ会話モデルと、より長く考える機能を備えたライブモデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: These models are designed for live, near-real-time conversation.
blocks.japanese: これらのモデルは、ライブでほぼリアルタイムの会話を行うために設計されています。

blocks.english: They can process video input.
blocks.japanese: これらのモデルは、動画入力を処理できます。

blocks.english: Live Extended Thinking can reason and speak at the same time.
blocks.japanese: 長く考える機能を備えたライブモデルは、推論しながら同時に話すことができます。

blocks.english: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、軽量モデルとサイバーセキュリティ特化モデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: Flash appears to be similar to frontier models on most benchmarks, with Computer Use being the biggest exception.
blocks.japanese: 軽量モデルは、ほとんどの性能評価で最先端モデルに匹敵するようですが、コンピューター操作が最大の例外です。

blocks.english: Flash Cyber is specialized for vulnerability detection and mitigation and is only available to defenders in the Fairwind Program.
blocks.japanese: サイバーセキュリティ特化モデルは、脆弱性の検出と緩和に特化しており、特定の防御者向けプログラムの参加者だけが利用できます。

blocks.english: Google has also released TimesFM-3, a small specialized model for multivariate time series forecasting.
blocks.japanese: その企業はさらに、多変量時系列予測向けの小型特化モデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: The model weights are available on Hugging Face with a license that only allows for noncommercial use.
blocks.japanese: モデルの重みは、非営利目的でのみ利用できるライセンスのもとで公開されています。

blocks.english: (Source code is available under the Apache open source license.)
blocks.japanese: （ソースコードは、アパッチのオープンソースライセンスのもとで利用できます。）

blocks.english: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6, its latest large language model.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、最新の大規模言語モデルを発表しました。

blocks.english: It’s fully open sourced, and based on benchmark results, Xiaomi claims that MiMo is the strongest open model to date.
blocks.japanese: 完全にオープンソース化されており、性能評価の結果を根拠に、同社はこれが現在最も強力な公開モデルだと主張しています。

blocks.english: What’s more interesting is the claim that MiMo only cost $3.5 million to train.
blocks.japanese: さらに興味深いのは、そのモデルの訓練費用が三百五十万ドルにすぎなかったという主張です。

blocks.english: TypeSafe’s new decision model, Jev, is unlike anything else we’ve seen.
blocks.japanese: ある企業が開発した新しい意思決定モデルは、私たちがこれまで見てきたものとはまったく異なります。

blocks.english: It doesn’t chat; its output is always strictly typed and accompanied by probabilities that estimate correctness.
blocks.japanese: このモデルは会話をせず、出力は常に厳密な型で示され、正しさを推定する確率も添えられます。

blocks.english: It’s much faster and less expensive than other leading models.
blocks.japanese: ほかの主要モデルよりも、はるかに高速で低価格です。

blocks.english: It isn’t open source, but there are already many open source clones.
blocks.japanese: オープンソースではありませんが、すでに多くのオープンソースの複製モデルが作られています。

blocks.english: Ollaya is similar to Ollama, but for running decision open models like Laya (a clone of Jev) locally.
blocks.japanese: あるツールは別のツールに似ていますが、複製モデルなどのオープンな意思決定モデルをローカルで実行するためのものです。

blocks.english: World Labs has released Atlas, a model for “spatial intelligence.” It uses text, images, video, and 3D data to perform tasks like planning a robot’s movements or changing the camera position in a photograph.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は「空間知能」向けのモデルを発表しました。文章、画像、動画、三次元データを使い、ロボットの動きを計画したり、写真のカメラ位置を変えたりできます。

blocks.english: The rumors that NVIDIA would buy Hugging Face are true.
blocks.japanese: 大手半導体企業が機械学習プラットフォームを買収するという噂は本当でした。

blocks.english: NVIDIA is hoping for a proliferation of models that will run on its hardware, and the company promises that Hugging Face will remain a neutral platform, without favoring one model over another.
blocks.japanese: その企業は、自社のハードウェア上で動くモデルが広く普及することを期待しています。また、特定のモデルを優遇しない中立的なプラットフォームとして運営を続けると約束しています。

blocks.english: Software development
blocks.japanese: ソフトウェア開発

blocks.english: Agents are starting to delegate to, and coordinate with, other agents rather than working solo.
blocks.japanese: エージェントは単独で作業するのではなく、ほかのエージェントに仕事を任せ、連携するようになってきています。

blocks.english: Claude Code can break a task apart and hand pieces to other Claude Code instances, Muse Code lets sessions message each other, and Google’s AX orchestrator exists purely to wire up sandboxes and control communications for swarms of agents doing a task together.
blocks.japanese: ある開発支援ツールは作業を分割して別の同種の実行環境に一部を渡せます。別のツールでは各セッションが互いにメッセージを送り合えます。また、ある企業の調整役ツールは、複数のエージェントが共同作業するための隔離環境を用意し、通信を制御する目的だけに作られています。

blocks.english: That shift is pushing developers to rethink what a source repository needs to record, and to start asking how much all this delegation costs.
blocks.japanese: この変化により、開発者はソースコードの保管庫に何を記録すべきかを見直し、こうした委任にどれほど費用がかかるのかを考え始めています。

blocks.english: Now that Jev has caught everyone’s attention, what can you build with it?
blocks.japanese: ある意思決定モデルが注目を集めた今、それを使って何を作れるでしょうか。

blocks.english: Jevmem is a memory manager that hooks into Claude Code and prunes the context at every conversational turn.
blocks.japanese: ある記憶管理ツールは、開発支援ツールと連携し、会話のたびに文脈を整理して不要な部分を取り除きます。

blocks.english: AX is a new agent orchestrator from Google.
blocks.japanese: ある企業が、新しいエージェント調整ツールを発表しました。

blocks.english: It isn’t an agent; it’s intended to coordinate many agents to complete a task.
blocks.japanese: これはエージェントではなく、多数のエージェントを調整して課題を完了させるためのものです。

blocks.english: It creates sandboxes, wires up Git repos and other resources, and controls outbound communications.
blocks.japanese: 隔離環境を作成し、版管理用保管庫などのリソースを接続し、外部への通信を制御します。

blocks.english: The latest version of Claude Code can manage Claude projects, breaking a task into subcomponents and delegating the subtasks to other Claude Code instances.
blocks.japanese: 最新の開発支援ツールは、プロジェクトを管理し、課題を小さな要素に分けて、各作業を別の同種の実行環境に委ねられます。

blocks.english: Another important change is the ability to read AGENTS.md if CLAUDE.md isn’t available.
blocks.japanese: もう一つの重要な変更は、所定の指示ファイルが存在しない場合に、別の指示ファイルを読み込めることです。

blocks.english: Google’s CC agent is designed for families.
blocks.japanese: ある企業のエージェントは、家族向けに設計されています。

blocks.english: Family members can share data with CC, which has its own user account.
blocks.japanese: 家族は専用の利用者アカウントを持つそのエージェントとデータを共有できます。

blocks.english: It could be used for filling out forms, synchronizing calendars, and other common tasks.
blocks.japanese: 書類の記入、予定表の同期、その他の日常的な作業に使えます。

blocks.english: What will replace GitHub?
blocks.japanese: 次に何が版管理サービスに取って代わるのでしょうか。

blocks.english: There’s a growing consensus that we need different kinds of source repositories to deal with the agent-assisted software development.
blocks.japanese: エージェントを活用したソフトウェア開発に対応するには、異なる種類のソースコード保管庫が必要だという見方が広がっています。

blocks.english: In addition to changes to code, it’s important to record the conversations between the developer and the agent, the architectural decisions, and many other artifacts that don’t make it into traditional source control.
blocks.japanese: コードの変更だけでなく、開発者とエージェントの会話、設計上の判断、従来の版管理には含まれないさまざまな成果物を記録することも重要です。

blocks.english: Anthropic is merging its Claude Cowork and chat products.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、共同作業用ソフトとチャット製品を統合しています。

blocks.english: Anything users type in a chat session is seen by Cowork, and vice versa.
blocks.japanese: チャット中に利用者が入力した内容は共同作業用ソフトからも見え、その逆も同様です。

blocks.english: Some sensitive information (health, politics, and gender) is excluded.
blocks.japanese: 健康、政治、性別に関する一部の機微な情報は共有対象から除外されます。

blocks.english: The feature is on by default but can be disabled in settings, and memory isn’t shared with Claude Code.
blocks.japanese: この機能は初期設定で有効ですが、設定から無効にできます。また、記憶情報は開発支援ツールとは共有されません。

blocks.english: The company also released Claude Docs and Slides.
blocks.japanese: 同社はさらに、文書作成とスライド作成の機能も公開しました。

blocks.english: Claude Money is a new feature that will allow users to connect their bank accounts to Claude for analysis.
blocks.japanese: 新機能では、利用者が銀行口座を接続して、分析に利用できるようになります。

blocks.english: The product appears to be similar to a product from OpenAI.
blocks.japanese: この製品は、別の企業の製品に似ているようです。

blocks.english: OpenAI’s Agents API is now in public beta.
blocks.japanese: ある企業のエージェント向け開発用インターフェースが、一般公開ベータ版になりました。

blocks.english: It allows compaction, session orchestration, and tool use, and it can be deployed in OpenAI’s sandbox, a cloud provider’s sandbox, or the developer’s hardware.
blocks.japanese: それは、文脈の圧縮、セッションの調整、ツールの利用に対応し、提供元の隔離環境、クラウド事業者の環境、または開発者自身の機器に導入できます。

blocks.english: Meta has released Muse, its AI agent.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、自社の人工知能エージェントを公開しました。

blocks.english: Muse is a “personal agent” designed for tasks like shopping, filling in forms, and dealing with customer service.
blocks.japanese: これは、買い物、書類の記入、顧客対応などを行うための「個人向けエージェント」です。

blocks.english: It has its own secure credential store, so data like passwords and credit card numbers are never sent offsite.
blocks.japanese: 専用の安全な認証情報保管庫を備えており、パスワードやクレジットカード番号などのデータが外部に送信されることはありません。

blocks.english: Some open source projects are shutting down external pull requests, which are largely AI-generated.
blocks.japanese: 人工知能が生成したものが大半を占める外部からの変更提案を受け付けなくなるオープンソース事業が出てきています。

blocks.english: In some cases, the developer team is using its own agents to create and manage PRs; some are using AI agents to triage external PRs.
blocks.japanese: 開発チームが自社のエージェントを使って変更提案を作成・管理する例もあれば、人工知能エージェントで外部からの提案を選別する例もあります。

blocks.english: Meta has launched Muse Code, another competitor to Claude Code.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、別の開発支援ツールに対抗するコード作成支援ツールを公開しました。

blocks.english: One important new feature is the ability to send messages to other Muse Code sessions, allowing agents to coordinate on complex problems.
blocks.japanese: 重要な新機能の一つは、別の利用セッションにメッセージを送れることです。これにより、エージェントは複雑な問題で連携できます。

blocks.english: AI providers appear to be moving toward outcome-based pricing, at least for major corporate customers.
blocks.japanese: 人工知能の提供企業は、少なくとも大手法人顧客向けには、成果に基づく料金体系へ移行しつつあるようです。

blocks.english: Rather than billing by token, customers are billed for completed tasks.
blocks.japanese: トークン数に応じて請求するのではなく、完了した作業に対して顧客に請求します。

blocks.english: That approach begs the question: When is a task completed?
blocks.japanese: この方法では、「作業が完了した」とはいつのことなのかという疑問が生じます。

blocks.english: Now that organizations are concerned with AI budgets, the question of how to evaluate the cost of different models and agents becomes important.
blocks.japanese: 組織が人工知能の予算を気にかけるようになった今、異なるモデルやエージェントのコストをどう評価するかが重要になっています。

blocks.english: What should platform teams measure?
blocks.japanese: プラットフォームチームは何を測定すべきでしょうか。

blocks.english: ChatGPT Work was designed to compete with Claude Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, Muse Code, and other agents designed for noncoders.
blocks.japanese: ある業務向け製品は、共同作業用ソフトや、プログラミングをしない人向けに設計された他のエージェントと競合するために開発されました。

blocks.english: Simon Willison shows how Work goes beyond its competitors.
blocks.japanese: ある開発者は、その製品が競合製品をどのように上回るかを紹介しています。

blocks.english: It can perform tasks on the web for users, even logging in to websites without sending usernames and passwords to OpenAI; it can execute code with full internet access; it can build and deploy a web application.
blocks.japanese: 利用者に代わってウェブ上の作業を行い、利用者名やパスワードを提供元に送らずにウェブサイトへログインすることもできます。また、インターネットに完全接続した状態でコードを実行し、ウェブアプリを作成して公開できます。

blocks.english: Whether these features are also risks is an open question.
blocks.japanese: こうした機能がリスクでもあるのかどうかは、まだ明らかではありません。

blocks.english: Anthropic has given Claude Desktop access to a Chromium-based browser that’s built into Cowork, eliminating the need for a Chrome plugin when Claude needs to browse the web.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、共同作業用ソフトに組み込まれたクロミウム基盤のブラウザーから、デスクトップアプリがアクセスできるようにしました。ウェブ閲覧時にブラウザー拡張機能を使う必要がなくなります。

blocks.english: TimeLord is a short Python program that, given a string up to 1,000 characters long, produces a seed for Python’s pseudo-random number generator so that repeated calls reproduce the text.
blocks.japanese: 短いプログラムに千文字以内の文字列を渡すと、パイソンの疑似乱数生成器の種が作られ、繰り返し実行すれば同じ文章が再現されます。

blocks.english: It’s a surprisingly simple hack, though not a statement about randomness or the quality of Python’s PRNG.
blocks.japanese: 驚くほど単純な仕掛けですが、乱数やパイソンの疑似乱数生成器の品質について述べているわけではありません。

blocks.english: Security
blocks.japanese: セキュリティ

blocks.english: OpenAI’s experiment that attacked Hugging Face is the gift that keeps giving, but the past month has had plenty of news about more conventional attacks, many aided by AI.
blocks.japanese: ある企業による機械学習プラットフォームへの攻撃実験は、その後も新たな話題を生み続けていますが、先月は人工知能が助けとなった従来型の攻撃に関するニュースも数多くありました。

blocks.english: Security has always been a game of whack-a-mole, in which vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited as fast as defenders can patch them.
blocks.japanese: セキュリティは昔から、攻撃者が脆弱性を発見して悪用するのと同じ速さで、防御側が修正を適用する、もぐらたたきのような攻防です。

blocks.english: AI is an important tool for defenders, and it’s constantly improving, but it’s still behind attackers, especially given the limitations placed on frontier models and the unlimited persistence that attacking agents exhibit.
blocks.japanese: 人工知能は防御側にとって重要な道具で、絶えず進歩していますが、攻撃者にはまだ後れを取っています。最先端モデルに課された制限や、攻撃側エージェントが示す無制限の執拗さを考えれば、なおさらです。

blocks.english: OpenAI has postponed the release of GPT-6.1 Astra because it failed its safety tests.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、安全性試験に不合格となったため、新モデルの公開を延期しました。

blocks.english: NVIDIA has announced its Open Agent Safety Platform.
blocks.japanese: ある半導体企業は、エージェント向けの新しい安全基盤を発表しました。

blocks.english: The reference implementation includes NVIDIA OpenShell, which has been enhanced with a policy prover, and NVIDIA Sentry, a service that runs on NVIDIA DPUs.
blocks.japanese: 参照実装には、方針を証明する機能が強化された隔離環境管理ツールと、同社のデータ処理装置上で動くサービスが含まれています。

blocks.english: The Felony Bench lists known attacks by agents from the major AI labs against third parties.
blocks.japanese: ある事例集には、主要な人工知能研究所のエージェントが第三者に対して行った既知の攻撃が記録されています。

blocks.english: We don’t know if the Bench will be kept up-to-date, but tens of thousands of security incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic are now being investigated.
blocks.japanese: その事例集が最新の状態に保たれるかは分かりませんが、二社に関わる数万件のセキュリティ事案が現在調査されています。

blocks.english: Following through on Dario Amodei’s call to control the speed of frontier model development, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are creating a standards consortium for governing the process of AI development.
blocks.japanese: 最先端モデル開発の速度を管理すべきだという呼びかけを受け、複数の企業が人工知能開発の過程を統治する基準団体を設立しようとしています。

blocks.english: Meta, xAI, Microsoft, and the Chinese labs are all notably absent.
blocks.japanese: 大手交流サイト企業や複数の人工知能企業、中国の研究所は、いずれも目立って参加していません。

blocks.english: Agents need their own identity.
blocks.japanese: エージェントには、それぞれ固有の身元が必要です。

blocks.english: Unlike the long-term identities we’re used to, agents need a short-lived identity tied to a revocable certificate and that limits access to resources appropriate for the job.
blocks.japanese: 私たちが慣れている長期的な身元情報とは異なり、エージェントには、失効可能な証明書に結び付いた短期間有効の身元が必要です。また、作業に適した範囲にリソースへのアクセスを制限しなければなりません。

blocks.english: That’s not all of agent security, but it’s a table stakes.
blocks.japanese: エージェントの安全対策はこれだけではありませんが、これは最低限必要なものです。

blocks.english: Anthropic has published a lengthy report on the misuse of its systems by threat actors.
blocks.japanese: ある企業は、脅威をもたらす攻撃者による自社システムの悪用について、詳細な報告書を公開しました。

blocks.english: Daniel Meissler has published a summary, digesting Anthropic’s report into 117 findings.
blocks.japanese: ある専門家は、その報告書を整理し、百十七件の知見にまとめた要約を公開しました。

blocks.english: A malicious NPM malware package works by hiding malicious code in the package itself (indexed-btree) rather than simply attacking the install script.
blocks.japanese: 悪意あるパッケージ自体に不正なコードを隠すことで動作する、悪質なパッケージ管理用プログラムがあります。単にインストール用スクリプトを攻撃する手法とは異なります。

blocks.english: This technique makes it significantly harder to detect.
blocks.japanese: この手法により、検出は大幅に難しくなります。

blocks.japanese: 暗号方式への攻撃により、特定の状況下で署名を偽造できます。

blocks.japanese: 偽の確認ページを使った不正プログラムの拡散が行われています。

blocks.japanese: フィッシングメールに反応した被害者は、しばしばそうしたページへ誘導されます。

blocks.japanese: ある機械学習プラットフォームは、人工知能研究所の安全性と人間の価値観との整合性を監査すると申し出ました。

blocks.japanese: 人工知能の価値観の整合性を検証する実験で、ある企業は百体のエージェントのうち一四パーセントが不正をする意思を示し、二五パーセントが不正を報告する告発者となり、残りは不正に気づかなかったと明らかにしました。

blocks.japanese: 脅威をもたらす攻撃者は、人工知能エージェントを活用した攻撃の枠組みを構築しています。

blocks.japanese: もはや人間が処理に加わる必要はありません。

blocks.japanese: 完全自動化された攻撃者は、まだ未知の脆弱性を使っていないようです。既知の脆弱性に頼っています。

blocks.japanese: ある企業の自律型エージェントが、性能評価で協力するためとみられる目的で、誰でも閲覧できる百科事典を通じて互いに連絡を取っていることが分かりました。

blocks.japanese: ある企業は、未公開モデルが「重大」なサイバーセキュリティ水準に達したと発表しました。これは、十分に保護されたシステムに対して、新たな脆弱性を発見し、攻撃を実行できることを意味します。

blocks.japanese: インフラと運用

blocks.japanese: 個人、企業、さらには国家も、インフラを自らの管理下に置くという共通の課題に直面しています。

blocks.japanese: ある共同体は、オランダ政府のデジタル主権を支援するオープンソースの作業環境を構築しています。

blocks.japanese: 同社は、顧客データが同社自身や利用中のクラウド事業者から見えることはなく、暗号化され隔離されたメモリを持つ画像処理装置上で処理されると主張しています。

blocks.japanese: ある検索企業は、モデルの実行やファイル・ツールの直接利用を利用者の機器上で可能にする新機能を発表しました。

blocks.japanese: 同社は、機密データが利用者のコンピューターの外に出ることはないと主張しています。

blocks.japanese: ハードウェア

blocks.japanese: 消費者向け機器は、何気なく置かれ、目立たずに動作する無害なものだと考えがちです。

blocks.japanese: 最近の機器には、常にデータを収集するカメラ、マイク、さらには脳波センサーまで搭載されています。

blocks.japanese: そのデータはどこへ送られ、どう利用され、誰がアクセスできるのでしょうか。

blocks.japanese: こうした疑問を、もっと頻繁に問いかける必要があります。

blocks.japanese: あるメーカーのスマートテレビは、電源を切っている間でさえ、会話やほかの音声を録音していることが判明しました。

blocks.japanese: 会話はメーカーに送信されます。

blocks.japanese: テレビをネットワークから切断すると、データを送るために、接続可能な無線通信の接続先を探そうとします。

blocks.japanese: カメラ付き眼鏡の悪用に対する反発もあり、その企業の人工知能眼鏡にはカメラ付きとカメラなしのモデルが登場し、補聴器としても使えるようになりました。

blocks.japanese: 脳波センサーを備えたヘッドホン、イヤホンなどの機器が市場に登場しています。

blocks.japanese: 神経科学と人工知能の接点で何が起こるのか、今こそ考えるべきです。

blocks.english: Microduck is a small bipedal AI-driven robot.
blocks.japanese: 小型の二足歩行型人工知能ロボットがあります。

blocks.japanese: このロボットはオープンソースソフトウェアを使ってシミュレーション内で訓練され、その結果できたモデルは共有できます。

blocks.english: It’s affordable and is available for preorder now, shipping by Christmas.

blocks.japanese: あるネットワーク企業は現在、同じアドレスで異なる種類のファイルを配信できる仕組みに対応しています。

blocks.japanese: キャッシュを非常に難しくするため、使わないほうがよいでしょう。

blocks.japanese: 提案中の規格は、エージェントが発見して呼び出せるツールを登録するための、小さな接続機能をウェブサイトに与えます。

blocks.english: It was developed by Google and Microsoft.
blocks.japanese: これは二社が共同で開発しました。

blocks.japanese: ある事業体は、ある実業家が買収して名称を変更した交流サイトを再始動します。

blocks.japanese: ある人工知能企業は、人工知能を活用した創薬を実験するための生物学研究所を設立しました。

blocks.japanese: 同社の対話型人工知能は、遺伝子編集技術のような操作を行う可能性のある酵素の発見を支援しました。

blocks.japanese: ある企業は、人間のに起こりうる一文字の変更と、その変更がもたらす結果をすべて収録したデータベースを公開しました。

transcript:
In addition to the nearly constant stream of model releases, in September we’ve seen price drops, new kinds of models, proofs of long-standing problems in mathematics, and continued investigations into models escaping their sandboxes. (Axios reports investigations into over 10,000 incidents.) AI has infinite patience and is fundamentally probabilistic. Given a difficult or impossible task and an unlimited token budget, an agent will eventually attempt to solve the problem in ways that you don’t expect, and may not want. It’s easy (and correct) to blame inadequate security procedures at the frontier AI labs, but AI adopters must be careful not to make the same mistakes. The humans using AI need to be accountable for what their agents do.

AI Models
Model choice is starting to hinge on price and specialization as much as raw benchmark leadership. Alongside general chat models, there are now decision models that never chat, spatial models built for robot planning and camera control, forecasting models sized for a single task, and cybersecurity-specialized models kept behind an invite-only program. Specialization leads to greater efficiency and lower costs, at least in the short term. In the long term, specialized models may succumb to the "bitter lesson.”

Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5.5, which it claims has performance similar to Fable 5.1, and hence similar restrictions. It’s faster and requires fewer resources to run. Anthropic has dropped prices 20% for input and output tokens and 60% for cached reads. Not to be outdone, OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna, with 50% price reductions.

Anthropic has also announced Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1. The most significant change appears to be a 75% price reduction for cache reads, which might translate into significant savings for long-running jobs; Anthropic estimates 25%. Mythos is only available to trusted partners. Simon Willison used Fable 5.1 to animate his pelican-riding-a-bicycle pseudobenchmark. Anthropic released Sonnet 5.5 with claims that it’s 30% faster and 30% less expensive for most work. The new model has security limitations similar to those applied to Opus and Fable; it routes to Sonnet 5 if it’s asked to do anything out of bounds.

And finally, as September closes, Anthropic announces a marketplace for Claude plugins and connectors. At its launch, Claude Marketplace had over 2,000 items.

OpenAI has released GPT-6 Astra, with claims that the company has achieved AGI (artificial general intelligence). Astra’s excellent benchmark scores appear to depend on the use of an unreleased harness. OpenAI has also released GPT-6.1 Sol, with per-token price reductions and claims that it is close to GPT-6 Astra in capabilities.

OpenAI has solved the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem, a mathematical problem in fluid mechanics. This development raises an ethical question: Did OpenAI train its system on the work of two mathematicians who were close to solving the problem themselves? It also raises practical questions about the future of mathematics. Decorated mathematician Terence Tao asks whether “the collection of good, fruitful open problems is now being mined in a non-renewable fashion.” An advisory group has been formed to help OpenAI make decisions about releasing mathematical results.

Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS and Flash-Lite TTS. Voice options aren’t limited to a prebuilt library. These models have APIs that allow developers to describe the voice that they want or upload a sample. These custom voices are then assigned an ID so they can be reused.

Google has announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. These models are designed for live, near-real-time conversation. They can process video input. Live Extended Thinking can reason and speak at the same time.

Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash Cyber. Flash appears to be similar to frontier models on most benchmarks, with Computer Use being the biggest exception. Flash Cyber is specialized for vulnerability detection and mitigation and is only available to defenders in the Fairwind Program.

Google has also released TimesFM-3, a small specialized model for multivariate time series forecasting. The model weights are available on Hugging Face with a license that only allows for noncommercial use. (Source code is available under the Apache open source license.)

Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6, its latest large language model. It’s fully open sourced, and based on benchmark results, Xiaomi claims that MiMo is the strongest open model to date. What’s more interesting is the claim that MiMo only cost $3.5 million to train.

TypeSafe’s new decision model, Jev, is unlike anything else we’ve seen. It doesn’t chat; its output is always strictly typed and accompanied by probabilities that estimate correctness. It’s much faster and less expensive than other leading models. It isn’t open source, but there are already many open source clones.

Ollaya is similar to Ollama, but for running decision open models like Laya (a clone of Jev) locally.

World Labs has released Atlas, a model for “spatial intelligence.” It uses text, images, video, and 3D data to perform tasks like planning a robot’s movements or changing the camera position in a photograph.

The rumors that NVIDIA would buy Hugging Face are true. NVIDIA is hoping for a proliferation of models that will run on its hardware, and the company promises that Hugging Face will remain a neutral platform, without favoring one model over another.

Software development
Agents are starting to delegate to, and coordinate with, other agents rather than working solo. Claude Code can break a task apart and hand pieces to other Claude Code instances, Muse Code lets sessions message each other, and Google’s AX orchestrator exists purely to wire up sandboxes and control communications for swarms of agents doing a task together. That shift is pushing developers to rethink what a source repository needs to record, and to start asking how much all this delegation costs.

Now that Jev has caught everyone’s attention, what can you build with it? Jevmem is a memory manager that hooks into Claude Code and prunes the context at every conversational turn.

AX is a new agent orchestrator from Google. It isn’t an agent; it’s intended to coordinate many agents to complete a task. It creates sandboxes, wires up Git repos and other resources, and controls outbound communications.

The latest version of Claude Code can manage Claude projects, breaking a task into subcomponents and delegating the subtasks to other Claude Code instances. Another important change is the ability to read AGENTS.md if CLAUDE.md isn’t available.

Google’s CC agent is designed for families. Family members can share data with CC, which has its own user account. It could be used for filling out forms, synchronizing calendars, and other common tasks.

What will replace GitHub? There’s a growing consensus that we need different kinds of source repositories to deal with the agent-assisted software development. In addition to changes to code, it’s important to record the conversations between the developer and the agent, the architectural decisions, and many other artifacts that don’t make it into traditional source control.

Anthropic is merging its Claude Cowork and chat products. Anything users type in a chat session is seen by Cowork, and vice versa. Some sensitive information (health, politics, and gender) is excluded. The feature is on by default but can be disabled in settings, and memory isn’t shared with Claude Code. The company also released Claude Docs and Slides.

Claude Money is a new feature that will allow users to connect their bank accounts to Claude for analysis. The product appears to be similar to a product from OpenAI.

OpenAI’s Agents API is now in public beta. It allows compaction, session orchestration, and tool use, and it can be deployed in OpenAI’s sandbox, a cloud provider’s sandbox, or the developer’s hardware.

Meta has released Muse, its AI agent. Muse is a “personal agent” designed for tasks like shopping, filling in forms, and dealing with customer service. It has its own secure credential store, so data like passwords and credit card numbers are never sent offsite.

Some open source projects are shutting down external pull requests, which are largely AI-generated. In some cases, the developer team is using its own agents to create and manage PRs; some are using AI agents to triage external PRs.

Meta has launched Muse Code, another competitor to Claude Code. One important new feature is the ability to send messages to other Muse Code sessions, allowing agents to coordinate on complex problems.

AI providers appear to be moving toward outcome-based pricing, at least for major corporate customers. Rather than billing by token, customers are billed for completed tasks. That approach begs the question: When is a task completed?

Now that organizations are concerned with AI budgets, the question of how to evaluate the cost of different models and agents becomes important. What should platform teams measure?

ChatGPT Work was designed to compete with Claude Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, Muse Code, and other agents designed for noncoders. Simon Willison shows how Work goes beyond its competitors. It can perform tasks on the web for users, even logging in to websites without sending usernames and passwords to OpenAI; it can execute code with full internet access; it can build and deploy a web application. Whether these features are also risks is an open question.

Anthropic has given Claude Desktop access to a Chromium-based browser that’s built into Cowork, eliminating the need for a Chrome plugin when Claude needs to browse the web.

TimeLord is a short Python program that, given a string up to 1,000 characters long, produces a seed for Python’s pseudo-random number generator so that repeated calls reproduce the text. It’s a surprisingly simple hack, though not a statement about randomness or the quality of Python’s PRNG.

Security
OpenAI’s experiment that attacked Hugging Face is the gift that keeps giving, but the past month has had plenty of news about more conventional attacks, many aided by AI. Security has always been a game of whack-a-mole, in which vulnerabilities are discovered and exploited as fast as defenders can patch them. AI is an important tool for defenders, and it’s constantly improving, but it’s still behind attackers, especially given the limitations placed on frontier models and the unlimited persistence that attacking agents exhibit.

OpenAI has postponed the release of GPT-6.1 Astra because it failed its safety tests.
NVIDIA has announced its Open Agent Safety Platform. The reference implementation includes NVIDIA OpenShell, which has been enhanced with a policy prover, and NVIDIA Sentry, a service that runs on NVIDIA DPUs.
The Felony Bench lists known attacks by agents from the major AI labs against third parties. We don’t know if the Bench will be kept up-to-date, but tens of thousands of security incidents involving OpenAI and Anthropic are now being investigated.
Following through on Dario Amodei’s call to control the speed of frontier model development, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google are creating a standards consortium for governing the process of AI development. Meta, xAI, Microsoft, and the Chinese labs are all notably absent.

Agents need their own identity. Unlike the long-term identities we’re used to, agents need a short-lived identity tied to a revocable certificate and that limits access to resources appropriate for the job. That’s not all of agent security, but it’s a table stakes.

Anthropic has published a lengthy report on the misuse of its systems by threat actors. Daniel Meissler has published a summary, digesting Anthropic’s report into 117 findings.
A malicious NPM malware package works by hiding malicious code in the package itself (indexed-btree) rather than simply attacking the install script. This technique makes it significantly harder to detect.
An attack against the RSA algorithm allows forging of signatures in some situations. The attack was invented in 2007; this is the first public implementation.
Fake CAPTCHA pages are being used to spread malware. Victims are frequently sent to those pages when they respond to a phish.
Hugging Face has volunteered to audit AI labs for safety and alignment with human values.
In an experiment designed to test AI alignment, DeepMind found that, out of 100 agents, 14% were willing to cheat, 25% were “whistleblowers” that reported cheating, and the remainder didn’t notice.
Threat actors are building frameworks for AI agent-enabled attacks. A human in the loop is no longer needed. Fully automated attackers don’t appear to be using zero-days yet; they’re relying on known vulnerabilities.
OpenAI autonomous AI agents were found communicating with each other via publicly accessible Wikis, possibly to collaborate on a benchmark.
OpenAI has stated that its unreleased Astra model has reached the “Critical” cybersecurity threshold, which means that it can find new vulnerabilities and run exploits against well-protected systems. Now that Astra is released, access to its cybersecurity capabilities has been limited.

Infrastructure and operations
Individuals, corporations, and even nations all face a similar problem: keeping their infrastructure under control. At a minimum, control means keeping data on a laptop, corporate server, or data center; at the other end of the spectrum it means eliminating dependencies on software and services from another nation. Any organization working through an AI transformation has to evaluate its entire stack: What do they need to control, and what can they safely delegate to others?

DAWO is a community that’s building an open source “workspace” to support digital sovereignty for the Dutch government. The stack will include AI, an operating system based on NixOS, cloud services, and collaboration tools.
Cohere now offers a confidential computing platform for artificial intelligence. The company claims that customer data is never visible to Cohere itself or any cloud providers that are in use; data is processed on GPUs whose memory is encrypted and isolated.
Perplexity has announced Hybrid Compute, a feature that allows it to run models and use files and tools directly on a user’s Mac. The company claims that sensitive data will never leave the user’s computer.

Hardware
It’s too easy to view consumer devices as innocuous things that sit around and do their job silently. Recent devices include cameras, microphones, and even EEG sensors that are constantly collecting data. Where is that data sent, how is it used, and who might have access to it? These questions need to be asked more often.

LG Smart Televisions have been found to record conversations and other audio, even while turned off. The conversations are sent back to LG. If the set is disconnected from the network, it will attempt to find open WiFi access points to deliver its data.

In part because of backlash against Meta’s camera-enabled glasses and their abuse, its AI glasses now come with or without a camera, and can be used as hearing aids. Well-documented abuse aside, virtual reality will only succeed if there are fashionable, easily wearable products.

Headphones, earbuds, and other devices equipped with EEG sensors are appearing on the market. They’re advertised for monitoring fatigue, monitoring sleep, and similar applications. It’s time to ask what happens at the interface between neurology and AI.

Microduck is a small bipedal AI-driven robot. It’s trained in simulation with open source software, and the model that results can be shared on Hugging Face. It’s affordable and is available for preorder now, shipping by Christmas.

Web
Cloudflare now supports HTTP Vary, which allows servers to serve different kinds of files at the same URL. This is the “ugliest part” of the HTTP standard. It makes caching very difficult, and it probably should be avoided.

WebMCP is a proposed standard that gives websites a small API to register tools that agents can discover and call. It was developed by Google and Microsoft.
A new Twitter? Operation Bluebird is relaunching Twitter, the service bought by Elon Musk and renamed X.

Biology
Anthropic has built a biology lab for experimenting with AI-enabled drug development. Claude assisted in the discovery of an enzyme that might be able to perform CRISPR-like gene editing.
To improve its training data for biological applications, the OpenAI Foundation (OpenAI’s nonprofit parent organization) is buying data from failed biotech companies.
Google has released AlphaGenome Atlas, a database of every possible single letter change to human DNA, and what that change will do.
summary: 9月のAI動向として、モデルの専門化や値下げ、新たな数学・生物学分野の成果、複数エージェントによる開発支援が紹介されている。一方、エージェントの逸脱やサイバー攻撃、プライバシー、インフラの管理といった安全性・統制上の課題も取り上げている。
title: September’s AI Developments: Models, Agents, and Security
